action_summary: Replaces a measurement that was wrong with one that says what it can and cannot see. The prior round reported CHECK_NO_TEST_MODULE for 6 of 12 real tasks; against the real repositories that verdict was a finder bug -- jodal/comics src/comics/accounts/models.py has five test files importing it, all missed because the finder globbed only test_*.py. The corrected finder searches four naming conventions and three graph kinds (imports, relative imports, packaging metadata, router dispatch): 74 changed files across six pinned repos give 18 of 54 non-test files with a reachable check (33 percent), not 0 of 42. It then separates reachability from adequacy by mutation: 3 of 5 mutants survived on two real projects, so a test that imports a module still does not catch a behavioural break. Finally measures claim D directly: carrying a learned model into drive() saves 0 of 1672 interactions, while validated replay saves 98.9 percent (18 interactions) -- and an unvalidated replay on a drifted world lands at (7,8,9) against a goal of (7,2,9). Adds no capability, trains nothing, claims no benchmark movement.

What is real and what is not, and what are the smartest things we can do?', 'you must think from first principles', 'kill all the bad and dumb ideas before you waste time implementing them', 'maximize your web use', and 'always after you make any of your work, push and merge your work always'. This PR answers the question with measurements and repairs the instrument that was too broken to measure with.
falsification_condition: Re-run the finder on the six pinned base SHAs and get fewer than 18 of 54 non-test files with a reachable check; or find a name-convention or graph kind it still misses on those repos; or find a mutant in the recorded set that the corresponding suite catches and this record says it did not.

obs_goal.surviving_necessity: One shot makes a lesson permanent exactly as well as it makes a mistake permanent, so the check is not adjacent to the claim, it is the claim.

recursive_obs.why_selected_route_is_fastest_sufficient: The claim could not be tested with the instrument that existed, because the instrument reported absence where it had only failed to look. Repairing it cost one afternoon of file reading and answered the claim directly; building a learner first would have produced a number nobody could check.
recursive_obs.stop_condition: The corrected number is recorded and the tool cannot claim adequacy it did not measure.

highest_leverage_reason: Every downstream claim about one-shot learning rests on being able to tell whether a change is wrong. The previous instrument could not, and reported that it could not when the real cause was that it was not looking. Fixing the instrument is the precondition for any measurement of claim D.
